recipes.title: Shared beef & vegetable base
recipes.intro: Cook once, then split between bolognese and chilli.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan. Soften the onion and carrot for 7–8 minutes.
Add the mince and brown thoroughly, breaking up any lumps. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Divide the cooked mixture equally. Use half in the bolognese and half in the chilli; finish both sauces now.
recipes.storage: Store the finished sauces using their recipe instructions.
recipes.note: The mince, onion and carrot here are already included in the shopping list. Do not buy them again for the two sauces.

recipes.title: Beef & lentil bolognese
recipes.intro: A familiar sauce with extra vegetables and red lentils.
ingredients: ½ of the cooked shared beef base
For this week’s plate: 75g dry pasta + 150g broccoli
steps: Make the shared beef base first and put half in a saucepan.
Add tomatoes, lentils, water, herbs and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender. Add a splash of water if the sauce gets too thick.
Split into 2 portions. On Monday, cook 75g pasta according to the packet and cook 150g broccoli; serve with 1 hot sauce portion.
recipes.storage: Saturday: cool both sauce portions promptly and freeze separately. Move Monday’s portion to the fridge on Sunday evening. Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. Keep the second portion for another week.
recipes.note: Open “Shared beef & vegetable base” for the first step. Pasta and broccoli are only allocated for this week’s serving.

recipes.title: Smoky beef & bean chilli
recipes.intro: A whole tin of kidney beans goes into this generous batch.
ingredients: ½ of the cooked shared beef base
1 × 400g tin kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 tsp ground cumin + 1 tsp smoked paprika
¼–½ tsp chilli powder, to taste
For this week’s plate: 70g dry rice + 200g broccoli
steps: Put half the cooked shared beef base in a pan.
Add the pepper, beans, tomatoes, water and spices.
Simmer for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pepper is tender. Split into 2 portions.
On Thursday, cook 70g dry rice according to the packet or rice cooker instructions and cook 200g broccoli. Serve with 1 hot chilli portion.
recipes.storage: Saturday: cool and freeze both sauce portions separately. Move Thursday’s portion to the fridge on Wednesday evening. Reheat once until steaming hot. Keep the other portion frozen for another week.
recipes.note: The shared beef base is a separate recipe. Cook dinner rice fresh; it is not the cold rice lunch.

recipes.title: Tomato chicken & chickpea curry
recipes.intro: A colourful curry using a full tin of chickpeas.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry paste of your choice
For this week’s plate: 70g dry rice + 150g broccoli
steps: Heat the oil. Soften the onion and carrot for 7–8 minutes.
Add chicken, pepper, garlic and curry paste. Stir for 3 minutes.
Add chickpeas, tomatoes and water. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender. Add water if needed.
Divide into 3 portions. On Tuesday, cook the rice according to its packet and cook the broccoli to serve with 1 portion.
recipes.storage: Sunday: cool and freeze all 3 curry portions. Move Tuesday’s portion to the fridge on Monday evening. Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. Leave the other 2 portions frozen.
recipes.note: Choose the heat level you enjoy. Check paste labels for allergens and storage instructions.

recipes.title: Smoky sausage & vegetable traybake
recipes.intro: One tray, familiar flavours and plenty of vegetables.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional.
Toss the potatoes and carrot with oil, paprika and pepper in a roasting tin. Roast for 15 minutes.
Add the sausages, onion and pepper. Roast for another 25–30 minutes, turning halfway, until the sausages are cooked through and vegetables are tender. Follow the sausage packet if it needs longer.
recipes.storage: Cook fresh on Wednesday. Freeze the unused raw sausages on shopping day, following the packet, and label them.
recipes.note: A little midweek cooking gives you a change from reheated batch meals.

recipes.title: Lemon white fishcakes
recipes.intro: Crisp breadcrumbs, soft potato and boneless white fish.
ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon + 1 tbsp lemon juice
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15–20 minutes until tender. Drain well and mash without milk. Let the mash cool.
Cook the fish according to its packet. Drain, check for any remaining bones and flake.
Combine fish, mash, lemon zest, juice and pepper. Shape into 4 large cakes and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Dip each cake in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Place on a lined tray and lightly brush with oil.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, turning carefully, until golden and hot throughout. Cool promptly if freezing.
On Friday, reheat 2 defrosted cakes at 180°C fan / 200°C conventional for about 20–25 minutes, until steaming hot throughout. Cook 160g peas and 150g carrots to serve.
recipes.storage: Saturday: cool and freeze all 4 cooked cakes, separated with baking paper in 2 packs of 2. Move Friday’s pack into the fridge Thursday evening. Reheat only once. Keep the other pair for another week.
recipes.note: The potato amounts are edible weights: buy a little extra if peeling produces substantial waste.

recipes.title: Lunch chicken prep
recipes.intro: Keeps raw and cooked chicken quantities clear.
ingredients: 500g raw chicken breast, divided into 3 roughly equal portions
½ tsp smoked paprika + black pepper
steps: On Sunday, put 1 raw portion (about 165g) into a labelled freezer bag, in thin strips, and freeze straight away for Friday’s noodles.
Heat the oven to 190°C fan / 210°C conventional. Coat the other 2 portions (about 335g raw in total) with oil, paprika and pepper.
Roast for about 20–25 minutes, until fully cooked throughout; thicker breasts may need longer.
Cool promptly and divide the cooked chicken equally between Monday’s Caesar pasta and Tuesday’s pesto pasta. Refrigerate the finished lunches.
recipes.storage: Prepare the two cooked portions on Sunday evening and eat within 48 hours. Defrost the raw Friday portion in the fridge from Wednesday evening; cook within 24 hours of being fully defrosted on Thursday.
recipes.note: Use separate utensils for raw chicken, and do not wash it. Fully cooked chicken should have no pink meat and juices should run clear; a food thermometer can confirm doneness.

recipes.title: Chicken Caesar pasta salad
recipes.intro: The Caesar you enjoy, made more filling with chicken, pasta and peas.
ingredients: 1 cooked portion from Lunch chicken prep
½ small romaine lettuce, washed and dried
steps: Cook the pasta according to its packet. Cook the peas, drain both and cool promptly.
Toast the bread cubes in a dry frying pan until crisp, then cool.
Combine pasta, peas, chicken and tomatoes in a lunch box. Mix Caesar dressing with yoghurt in a small separate pot.
Pack dry lettuce, Parmesan and croutons separately or in separate compartments to preserve their texture. Refrigerate. Combine at lunchtime.
recipes.storage: Make Sunday evening and eat Monday. Keep the lunch chilled at work or use an insulated bag with ice packs.
recipes.note: No preparation before work. The dressing and croutons are packed the night before.

recipes.title: Creamy pesto chicken pasta
recipes.intro: Creamy pesto, chicken and tomatoes, with a crunchy side.
ingredients: 1 cooked portion from Lunch chicken prep
A squeeze of lemon or a little water
steps: Cook the pasta and peas, drain and cool promptly.
Stir together pesto and yoghurt, loosening with a little water or lemon juice.
Combine the sauce with pasta, peas, chicken and tomatoes. Pack carrot sticks alongside and refrigerate.
recipes.storage: Make Sunday evening and eat Tuesday lunchtime, within 48 hours of preparation. Keep chilled during travel and at work.
recipes.note: Freeze leftover pesto in small portions if the jar’s opened storage life would otherwise be exceeded.

recipes.title: Egg & potato Caesar salad
recipes.intro: A second take on Caesar with eggs, potatoes and peas.
ingredients: ½ small romaine lettuce, washed and dried
steps: Boil potatoes for about 12–15 minutes until tender; drain and cool. In another pan, boil the eggs for 10–12 minutes until hard-boiled, cool in cold water and peel.
Cook the peas and cool promptly. Toast the bread cubes in a dry pan and cool.
Mix the Caesar dressing and yoghurt in a separate pot. Pack potato, peas, quartered eggs and tomatoes together, with dry lettuce and Parmesan alongside.
Pack the dressing, croutons and carrot sticks. Refrigerate everything except the dry croutons. Combine at lunch.
recipes.storage: Prepare Tuesday evening and eat Wednesday. Keep chilled; do not freeze the assembled salad.

recipes.title: Cold egg-fried rice
recipes.intro: A simple rice box with eggs, peas and carrot.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet or rice cooker instructions.
In a frying pan, soften carrot and peas with a splash of water. Let excess water evaporate.
Add sesame oil and eggs; stir until the egg is fully set. Stir in the cooked rice and soy sauce.
Immediately spread into a clean, shallow container to cool quickly. Refrigerate within 1 hour of cooking. Do not leave it in the rice cooker to cool.
recipes.storage: Make Wednesday evening and eat cold on Thursday, within 24 hours of cooking. Keep refrigerated, including at work; use ice packs for the journey. This lunch is not intended for batch fridge storage.
recipes.note: Rice has a shorter storage window than the other lunches. Only cook this lunch the evening before.

recipes.title: Chicken chow mein noodle salad
recipes.intro: The whole tin of beansprouts goes in: no half-tin left behind.
ingredients: 1 standard tin beansprouts, drained (use the whole tin)
½ tsp dark soy sauce, optional
½ tsp sesame oil + 1 tsp cooking oil
steps: Cook the egg noodles according to their packet and drain.
Heat the cooking oil in a frying pan or wok. Stir-fry the chicken strips until fully cooked throughout.
Add the onion, carrot and the whole drained tin of beansprouts. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, following any extra cooking instruction on the tin.
Toss with noodles, soy sauces, sesame oil and lemon. Transfer to a shallow container, cool promptly and refrigerate.
recipes.storage: Move the frozen raw chicken to the fridge Wednesday evening. Cook this lunch Thursday evening, within 24 hours of the chicken being fully defrosted. Eat Friday, kept chilled.
recipes.note: If your tin is especially large, this is a very generous lunch. The plan deliberately uses all of it.

recipes.title: Berry & walnut overnight oats
recipes.intro: Prep in the evening; grab from the fridge in the morning.
steps: Check frozen berry packaging: if it says to cook before eating, cook the berries as directed and cool promptly first.
Mix oats, yoghurt, berries and a splash of water in a covered container. Refrigerate overnight.
Pack walnuts in a small pot or sprinkle on top in the evening. Eat the next morning.
recipes.storage: Prepare the evening before, rather than making all five at once. Follow yoghurt and berry storage labels.
recipes.note: Buy 200g oats, 750g yoghurt, 400g berries and 75g walnuts for five breakfasts. Add one apple or banana each day.

week: Move Tuesday’s curry into the fridge. Make overnight oats.
Make Wednesday’s egg & potato salad and oats.
Make Thursday’s rice lunch and oats. Move chilli and raw noodle chicken into the fridge.
Cook Friday’s noodles and make oats. Move 2 fishcakes into the fridge.
Enjoy your dinner; 5 extra main-meal portions are ready for another week.
prep: Tick anything you already have on the shopping list before buying. Check dates on chicken, fish, sausages and yoghurt.
Freeze extra raw sausages and bread. Keep larger frozen packs frozen. Allow room for shallow containers and label them.
Finish both bolognese and chilli sauces. Cool and freeze all 4 portions individually.
Bake all 4. Cool and freeze in 2 packs of 2. Label each pack with its name and cooking date.
Divide into 3 portions. Cool promptly and freeze all three.
Cook 2 portions for Monday and Tuesday. Freeze the third portion RAW, sliced, for Friday’s noodles.
Make Caesar pasta and pesto pasta. Keep dressings/croutons separate where directed. Refrigerate; eat within 48 hours.
Move Monday’s bolognese to the fridge
Thaw in a covered container. Make Monday’s oats.
Move one portion to the fridge.
Check the yoghurt’s opened storage instructions.
Pack the egg & potato Caesar salad
Boil eggs and potatoes, cook peas, cool and pack. Keep croutons and dressing separate.
While the oven is on, prepare Thursday’s rice lunch.
Cool and refrigerate within 1 hour. Eat within 24 hours.
Move Thursday’s chilli and Friday’s raw chicken portion into the fridge. Keep raw chicken covered below ready-to-eat food.
Pack an apple or banana too.
Use the defrosted raw chicken and the WHOLE tin of beansprouts. Cool promptly and refrigerate.
Move one pack of 2 cakes to the fridge.
Keep lunch chilled during travel and at work.
Reheat 2 fishcakes and cook the sides
There should be 1 bolognese, 1 chilli, 2 curry portions and 1 fishcake dinner left if you cooked the complete plan. Update your actual stock in the Freezer section.
